projectName: Robotics Lab Equipment Booking and Tracking System
oneLineSummary: A role-based laboratory operations system for managing robotics equipment, bookings, availability, incidents, and daily admin workflows.

summary.systemDefinition: A university lab equipment management platform built for students, staff, and administrators interacting with shared robotics equipment.
coreWorkflowsFeatures: Equipment listing, equipment profiles, and availability visibility
Booking requests, approvals, cancellations, returns, and booking calendar views
Incident reporting, due-item notifications, and dashboard reminders for daily operations
summary.businessOrOperationalImpact: The system streamlines equipment management, reduces booking friction, improves visibility into equipment usage, and creates a more organised incident-handling process for the lab.
summary.engineeringValue: It demonstrates role-based workflow design, layered Spring application architecture, controller-service-repository separation, and quality practices including CI and unit testing.

projectNarrative.problem: The robotics lab needed a more organised way to manage equipment lending, booking approvals, incident reports, and day-to-day administrative follow-up across different user roles.
projectNarrative.approach: Our team designed and implemented a layered web system with separate student, staff, and admin workflows, backed by booking, equipment, incident, login, and notification controllers and services.
projectNarrative.result: The project produced a structured internal tool for lab equipment operations and gave the team a practical framework for coordinating bookings, incidents, notifications, and equipment tracking in one system.

engineeringHighlights: Role-based workflow support for students, staff, and administrators
Layered architecture spanning interface, controller, model, and database layers
Controller-service-repository design in Spring Boot with multiple domain modules
Booking, incident, notification, and dashboard workflow implementation
CI pipeline setup and unit testing coverage across bookings, incidents, notifications, dashboard, equipment, login, and users

reflection.tradeoffs: Supporting multiple user roles and operational states in one system required clear workflow boundaries so booking, incident, and dashboard logic stayed understandable as the project grew.
lessonsLearned: Role-based internal tools benefit from explicit controller and service boundaries early.
Operational dashboards are most useful when tied directly to concrete daily actions.
Testing and CI become more important as booking, notification, and equipment workflows start overlapping.
futureImprovements: Expand notification reliability and due-item automation
Polish unfinished features and improve production readiness
